holidays.name: International Chocolate Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to indulging in all things cocoa, from silky truffles to gooey brownies. Chocolate lovers worldwide unwrap their favorite treats and guiltlessly celebrate.
holidays.origin: Often tied to September 13 as the birthday of Milton S. Hershey, founder of the Hershey Chocolate Company, born in 1857 in Pennsylvania.
holidays.funFact: Cacao beans were once used as currency by the Aztecs, so technically you are spending money when you eat chocolate.

holidays.name: Fortune Cookie Day
holidays.description: A day to crack open a crispy cookie and read your fortune, then add the traditional 'in bed' at the end for extra giggles.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance celebrating the crunchy treat that ends so many Chinese-American restaurant meals. Its roots trace to early 20th-century California.
holidays.funFact: Fortune cookies are not traditional in China; they were popularized in the United States, and Japanese-American bakers in California likely made them first.

holidays.name: Positive Thinking Day
holidays.description: A day to banish negativity and look at the bright side of life. Participants are encouraged to flip their frowns upside down and spread optimism.
holidays.origin: An unofficial awareness day created to promote optimism and the idea that positive thoughts can influence outcomes, inspired by self-help movements like Norman Vincent Peale's 'The Power of Positive Thinking' (1952).
holidays.funFact: Studies on optimism suggest that optimistic people may enjoy better heart health and even longer lives than pessimists.

holidays.name: Grandparents Day (Observed Around This Time in Some Countries)
holidays.description: A celebration of grandparents, with hugs, hard candies, and stories from the good old days. Younger generations show appreciation for their elders' wisdom and spoiling skills.
holidays.origin: In the U.S., National Grandparents Day was signed by President Jimmy Carter in 1978 and falls on the first Sunday after Labor Day, which often lands near September 13.
holidays.funFact: Marian McQuade, the West Virginia housewife who championed the holiday, reportedly campaigned for it for years before it became official.

holidays.name: Kiss Your Mate Day
holidays.description: A smooch-heavy observance encouraging couples to take a moment, pucker up, and show affection to their partner just because.
holidays.origin: An informal, lighthearted observance in the family of quirky calendar holidays encouraging daily romance beyond Valentine's Day.
holidays.funFact: The average person spends about two weeks of their life kissing, according to popular estimates.
